newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-West spot electricity holds steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-West spot electricity holds steady.

text.p: U.S. Mid-West spot electricity held steady Tuesday with the thin demand for short term power sending many players out searching for longer-term deals, industry sources said.
On-peak, non-firm next day power for Wednesday delivery in the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP) was pegged steady in the 15.00-15.50 range, the sources said.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power was pegged steady in the $8.00-9.00 range.
On-peak non-firm prices in the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN) for Wednesday delivery were also talked steady at $17.50-18.50 per megawatt hour (MWh).
Off-peak non-firm MAIN power was said to be steady in the $11.00-12.50 range.
November MAIN electricity was said to be steady in the $19.00-19.50 range for delivery of a peak 16-hour block through the five business days of the week.
In the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR), peak non-firm power prices for Wednesday were said to be holding at $16.00-18.50.
Off peak non-firm ECAR was said to be steady at $12.00-13.50.
November ECAR was said to be discussed unchanged near $17.00-18.00.
In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP), on-peak non-firm power for next-day delivery in the south of the region was assessed at $17.00-19.00, the sources said.
November SPP was discussed at $19.50-20.50 per MWh.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
